question: In which year did Nepal adopt its first democratic constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2015.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution of Nepal was endorsed on **September 16, 2015,** by the Constituent Assembly meeting by more than two-thirds majority.
 
• It states Nepal as a federal democratic republican nation.
 
• The executive rights of the country are stated to have belonged to the Council of Ministers while the President would be ceremonial head-of-the-state. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Nepal is a country accustomed to autocracy and lacking in democratic heritage and experience.
 
• Due to Civil disobedience campaigns in February 1959 due to this political development king was ready to hold the election in Nepal and draft a constitution for the country. 
 
• After the death of King Tribhuvan death in 19, his son Mahendra Bir Bikram shah succeeded the throne.
 
• King Mahendra drafted a constitution a week before the election and delivered presented to the nation.
 
• Royal Democratic Constitution was granted by king Mahendra rather than the constituent assembly
 
• Therefore, In the year 1959, the Royal Democratic Constitution of Nepal was drafted by Raja Mahendra.
